questions.question: Long before any European ship arrived, Polynesian voyagers settled Hawaii after crossing the Pacific using mainly:
questions.correctAnswer: Double-hulled voyaging canoes guided by stars, swells and seabirds
distractors: Horse caravans crossing a land bridge
questions.explanation: Polynesian settlers reached Hawaii in double-hulled canoes, navigating by the stars, ocean swells, winds and the flight of seabirds - no instruments or charts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Star, swell and bird: the first navigators' only tools.

questions.question: In pre-contact Hawaii, the system of laws and sacred rules that ordered daily life, fishing seasons and worship was called:
questions.correctAnswer: The kapu system
questions.explanation: Kapu were sacred rules set by the ali'i and priests: they governed eating, worship, fishing and contact between ranks, and breaking kapu could be punished by death.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Kapu: the sacred rules everyone lived by.

questions.question: A pie-shaped land division running from the mountains to the sea, designed so one community could reach upland forest, farmland and reef resources, was an:
questions.correctAnswer: Ahupua'a
questions.explanation: Ahupua'a divisions ran mauka to makai - mountain to sea - giving each community access to timber, taro land, fresh water and fishing grounds inside one unit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mountain to sea in one slice: ahupua'a.

img.scene: Aerial view of a Hawaiian valley running from green mountain ridges down through terraced fields to a reef and the ocean. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Mountain to sea in one slice: ahupua'a.
img.title: AHUPUA'A

questions.question: The staple food plant grown in flooded terraces called lo'i in old Hawaii was:
questions.correctAnswer: Kalo (taro)
questions.explanation: Kalo was the staff of life, grown in irrigated lo'i terraces; its corm was pounded into poi, and Hawaiian tradition links kalo to the ancestor Haloa.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Kalo in the lo'i, poi on the table.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Kalo in the lo'i, poi on the table.
img.title: KALO AND LO'I

questions.question: Hawaiians engineered walled ponds along the shore to raise fish such as mullet. These were:
questions.correctAnswer: Fishponds (loko i'a)
questions.explanation: Loko i'a fishponds, some hundreds of acres across, trapped and raised fish behind stone walls - one of the most advanced aquaculture systems in the ancient Pacific.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Stone walls that farmed the sea: loko i'a.

questions.question: Kamehameha was born on the island of:
questions.correctAnswer: Hawaii Island (the Big Island)
questions.explanation: Kamehameha was born around 1758 in Kohala on Hawaii Island; tradition ties his birth to the appearance of Halley's Comet, read as a sign of a great chief.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Born on the biggest island: Hawaii Island.

questions.question: Kamehameha's rise began in 1782 when he won control of part of Hawaii Island at the battle of:
questions.correctAnswer: Mokuohai
questions.explanation: After the death of Kalaniopuu, fighting between Kamehameha and Keoua and Kiwalao ended at Mokuohai in 1782, leaving Kamehameha holding the western and northern districts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mokuohai, 1782: the first step.

questions.question: In 1790 Kamehameha invaded Maui and won a bloody victory in Iao Valley at the battle called:
questions.correctAnswer: Kepaniwai - the damming of the waters
questions.explanation: Kepaniwai ('the damming of the waters') in Iao Valley, 1790, was so costly in lives that the stream was said to be choked; it broke Maui's resistance to Kamehameha.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Iao Valley, 1790: Kepaniwai.

questions.question: The 1795 battle that completed Kamehameha's conquest of Oahu, where defenders were driven over the cliff, was the battle of:
questions.correctAnswer: Nu'uanu
questions.explanation: At Nu'uanu in 1795, Kamehameha's army pushed Kalanikupule's forces up the valley to the pali (cliff); the victory gave him Oahu, Maui, Molokai and Lanai.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nu'uanu, 1795: Oahu falls.

questions.question: Kauai and Niihau joined Kamehameha's kingdom in 1810 in a different way than the other islands - they came in by:
questions.correctAnswer: Peaceful agreement with Kaumuali'i, Kauai's king
questions.explanation: After two invasion attempts failed (storm and disease), Kaumuali'i negotiated in 1810: Kauai kept its own king as governor under Kamehameha, uniting the islands without a Kauai battle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Kauai joined by talk, not war: 1810.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Kauai joined by talk, not war: 1810.
img.title: KAUAI JOINS BY PEACE

questions.question: Kamehameha's famous Kanawai Mamalahoe - the Law of the Splintered Paddle - protected:
questions.correctAnswer: Noncombatants: the elderly, women and children on the roads
questions.explanation: After a raid in which a fisherman struck his leg with a paddle, Kamehameha decreed that the aged, women and children could lie by the roadside in safety - a landmark early human-rights law.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Let the old and the young lie safe by the road.

questions.question: In 1778, the first Europeans known to reach Hawaii, led by this captain, arrived during the Makahiki season:
questions.correctAnswer: Captain James Cook
questions.explanation: Cook's ships Resolution and Discovery reached Kauai and Niihau in January 1778; he named the group the Sandwich Islands and returned the following winter.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1778: Cook's ships reach Kauai.

questions.question: Captain Cook died in 1779 at Kealakekua Bay after:
questions.correctAnswer: A violent clash with Hawaiians over a stolen boat
distractors: An outbreak of fever aboard ship
A duel with his own officer
questions.explanation: When a ship's boat was stolen, Cook went ashore to seize Kalaniopuu as hostage; the confrontation at Kealakekua turned violent and Cook and several others were killed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Kealakekua, 1779: the visit turned deadly.

questions.question: Foreign ships first came to Hawaii in large numbers because the islands were a perfect stopover for the trade in:
questions.correctAnswer: Sandalwood, furs and provisions for the China trade
questions.explanation: Hawaii sat on the route of the fur and sandalwood trade to Canton: chiefs traded fragrant sandalwood and supplies for foreign goods, arms and ships.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sandalwood for China: the first trade boom.

img.scene: Stacks of fragrant sandalwood logs being loaded into a sailing ship at a Hawaiian harbor, chiefs supervising workers. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Sandalwood for China: the first trade boom.

questions.question: Heavy sandalwood cutting in the early 1800s hurt ordinary Hawaiians mainly because:
questions.correctAnswer: Chiefs forced commoners into the mountains to cut wood, neglecting farms and food supply
distractors: The wood was all burned for fuel
Ships refused to pay for it
It made the forests grow back too fast
questions.explanation: The sandalwood debt economy pulled maka'ainana labor off the land; food production fell and commoners suffered while chiefs owed foreign merchants for imported goods.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sandalwood debt starved the farms.

img.scene: Weary Hawaiian workers carrying sandalwood logs down a forested mountain trail above neglected taro terraces, dignified and somber. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.

questions.question: In 1819, months after Kamehameha's death, his son Liholiho, urged by Ka'ahumanu and Keopuolani, publicly broke the eating kapu in the event called:
questions.correctAnswer: The 'Ai Noa - free eating
questions.explanation: At the 'Ai Noa ('free eating'), Kamehameha II ate with women, ending the kapu system; temples and images were destroyed across the kingdom - before any missionary arrived.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1819: the king ate with women, and kapu fell.

questions.question: Ka'ahumanu, Kamehameha's favorite wife, held real governing power after his death in the office of:
questions.correctAnswer: Kuhina Nui - co-ruler and regent
questions.explanation: As kuhina nui, Ka'ahumanu shared executive authority with the young kings, drove the end of the kapu system, and shaped law in the kingdom for over a decade.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ka'ahumanu: co-ruler, not just queen.

questions.question: The first company of American Protestant missionaries reached Hawaii in the year:
questions.explanation: The ABCFM company sailed from Boston in 1819 and reached Hawaii in spring 1820 - arriving, by chance, just after the kapu system had been abolished.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1820: the missionaries land.

questions.question: Missionaries and Hawaiian leaders together created a written form of Hawaiian, which led within a generation to:
questions.correctAnswer: One of the highest literacy rates in the world
distractors: The end of the Hawaiian language
questions.explanation: Hiram Bingham and others devised a Hawaiian alphabet; the kingdom built schools and presses, and by mid-century Hawaiian literacy was famously among the world's highest.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A written language, a literate kingdom.

img.scene: Hawaiian children and adults reading large printed books and newspapers in an open-air school under a banyan tree. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.

questions.question: The Hawaiian-language press mattered to the kingdom because newspapers carried:
questions.correctAnswer: News, laws, history and mo'olelo recorded by Hawaiians themselves
questions.explanation: From Ka Lama Hawaii (1834) onward, Hawaiian newspapers preserved laws, chiefly histories and thousands of pages of traditional knowledge written by Native Hawaiians.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Hawaiian press wrote Hawaii's own record.

img.scene: A 19th-century printing press in Lahaina with Hawaiian printers setting type, stacks of newspapers beside them. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The Hawaiian press wrote Hawaii's own record.

questions.question: The long-reigning third king, who ruled from 1825 to 1854 and gave Hawaii its first written constitution, was:
questions.correctAnswer: Kamehameha III (Kauikeaouli)
questions.explanation: Kauikeaouli, Kamehameha III, reigned nearly 30 years - the longest of any Hawaiian monarch - issuing the 1839 Declaration of Rights and the 1840 Constitution.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Third king, longest reign, first constitution.

img.scene: A young Hawaiian king in 19th-century royal dress reviewing a written document at a desk in a palace room, feather cloak over his chair. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Third king, longest reign, first constitution.
img.title: KAMEHAMEHA III

questions.question: Hawaii's motto, 'Ua mau ke ea o ka aina i ka pono' - the life of the land is perpetuated in righteousness - dates from 1843, when:
questions.correctAnswer: Admiral Thomas restored the kingdom after a British captain had seized it
questions.explanation: Lord Paulet seized Hawaii in 1843; Rear Admiral Thomas undid the seizure five months later, and Kamehameha III spoke the famous words at the thanksgiving service in Honolulu.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: July 31, 1843: sovereignty restored.

img.scene: A Hawaiian flag being raised again over Honolulu in 1843 before a crowd in a public square, a British warship departing in the harbor. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: July 31, 1843: sovereignty restored.
img.title: RESTORATION DAY 1843

questions.question: In November 1843, Britain and France jointly recognized Hawaii as an independent state in the:
questions.correctAnswer: Anglo-Franco Proclamation
questions.explanation: The Anglo-Franco Proclamation (Nov 28, 1843) pledged both powers to treat Hawaii as independent - making Hawaii one of the first non-Western states recognized as sovereign.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1843: the world recognized Hawaii.

img.scene: Two European diplomats and Hawaiian envoys exchanging sealed documents in a formal room, a world map on the wall without labels. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: 1843: the world recognized Hawaii.
img.title: RECOGNIZED INDEPENDENT

questions.question: Nineteenth-century Hawaiian kings sent envoys around the world mainly to win:
questions.correctAnswer: Treaties and formal recognition of the kingdom's independence
questions.explanation: Envoys like Timoteo Haalilio and William Richards secured treaties and recognition from the US, Britain and France - diplomacy was the small kingdom's shield.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Diplomacy was the kingdom's shield.

img.scene: Hawaiian envoys in formal 19th-century dress presenting credentials in an elegant European state room. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Diplomacy was the kingdom's shield.

questions.question: The Great Mahele of 1848 was a division of:
questions.correctAnswer: Land - ending the old system where all land belonged to the king and was held through chiefs
questions.explanation: The Mahele divided interests in every acre among the king, the government and the konohiki; a follow-on Kuleana Act let commoners claim the plots they farmed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1848: the land itself was divided.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: 1848: the land itself was divided.
img.title: THE GREAT MAHELE

questions.question: After the Mahele, the share of land that ended up as small kuleana awards to commoners was:
questions.correctAnswer: Less than one percent of the kingdom's land
questions.explanation: Although the Kuleana Act (1850) promised commoners their cultivated plots, claims required surveys, fees and paperwork in English-style proceedings; kuleana awards totaled under 1% of the land.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Promised plots, tiny awards: under one percent.

img.scene: A single small taro plot marked with survey stakes in a vast valley of large estates, a Hawaiian family standing by their plot. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Promised plots, tiny awards: under one percent.
img.title: KULEANA AWARDS

questions.question: The 1850 change that let foreigners buy and own Hawaiian land outright mattered because:
questions.correctAnswer: Land could now pass permanently out of Hawaiian hands through ordinary sales and foreclosures
distractors: It banned all land sales for a century
It returned crown lands to commoners
questions.explanation: Fee-simple ownership plus foreign purchase rights meant land became a commodity; over the following decades most land concentrated in government, crown and large private - often foreign - estates.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Land became property that could be lost for good.

img.scene: Deeds and survey maps spread on a table while a land agent and a Hawaiian family look on in a 19th-century land office. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Land became property that could be lost for good.
img.title: LAND BECOMES A COMMODITY

questions.question: Hawaii's population fell catastrophically during the first century of foreign contact mainly because of:
questions.correctAnswer: Introduced diseases against which Hawaiians had no immunity
questions.explanation: Measles, influenza, smallpox, venereal disease and other introduced illnesses cut the Native Hawaiian population from hundreds of thousands to under 50,000 by the late 1800s.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Disease, not war, emptied the villages.

img.title: POPULATION DECLINE

questions.question: From the 1840s to the 1860s, Honolulu and Lahaina grew rich as ports serving hundreds of ships a year from the Pacific fleet hunting:
questions.correctAnswer: Whales
questions.explanation: Whaling ships wintered in Hawaii for provisions, repairs and crew rest; whaling was the kingdom's second great maritime economy after sandalwood.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Whalers wintered in Lahaina and Honolulu.

img.scene: A harbor full of whaling ships at anchor in Lahaina roads with Maui mountains behind, sailors rowing ashore. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Whalers wintered in Lahaina and Honolulu.
img.title: WHALING PORTS

questions.question: The first successful sugar plantation, founded at Koloa on Kauai in 1835 by Ladd & Company, began an industry that would:
questions.correctAnswer: Reshape Hawaii's land, water and population for the next century
questions.explanation: Koloa plantation proved sugar could pay; plantations soon demanded land leases, irrigation works and imported labor, transforming the islands' economy and demography.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Koloa 1835: sugar changes everything.

img.scene: Green sugarcane fields at Koloa on Kauai with a small early mill building and an irrigation ditch in the foreground. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Koloa 1835: sugar changes everything.

questions.question: Plantations imported workers from many countries mainly because:
questions.correctAnswer: Native Hawaiian population decline left too few workers for the labor plantations demanded
distractors: Sugar could only be cut by hand overseas
questions.explanation: Falling Native population and booming acreage drove recruitment: Chinese (1852), Japanese, Portuguese, Puerto Rican, Korean and Filipino workers remade Hawaii's population.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fewer Hawaiians, more cane: labor came from abroad.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Fewer Hawaiians, more cane: labor came from abroad.

questions.question: The Reciprocity Treaty of 1876 between Hawaii and the United States gave Hawaiian sugar:
questions.correctAnswer: Duty-free entry into the US market, in exchange for Hawaii promising its ports and territory to no other power
distractors: A US military base at Pearl Harbor immediately
Free entry for American rice only
questions.explanation: Reciprocity (1876) boomed the sugar economy and bound Hawaii to the US commercially; the 1887 renewal added exclusive US rights to Pearl Harbor.

questions.question: Kamehameha IV and his wife Emma are remembered in Hawaii especially for founding:
questions.correctAnswer: The Queen's Hospital, to care for Native Hawaiians
questions.explanation: Seeing his people's numbers fall, Alexander Liholiho (Kamehameha IV) and Queen Emma raised funds for the hospital that opened in 1859 and still serves as The Queen's Medical Center.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A king and queen who built a hospital.

questions.question: Lunalilo, who became king in 1873, was distinctive because he was:
questions.correctAnswer: The first king chosen by popular election of the people
questions.explanation: William Charles Lunalilo insisted on a popular vote before the legislature confirmed him in 1873 - the first, and most democratic, royal succession in the kingdom.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lunalilo let the people choose.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Lunalilo let the people choose.

questions.question: Kalakaua, elected king in 1874, worked to revive Hawaiian culture - for example by:
questions.correctAnswer: Restoring hula to public life and recording the Kumulipo creation chant
questions.explanation: The 'Merrie Monarch' revived hula and chant after decades of suppression, built Iolani Palace, traveled the world and had the Kumulipo genealogy published.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Merrie Monarch brought hula back.

img.scene: Hula dancers performing proudly at a royal birthday celebration on palace grounds in the 1880s, musicians with gourd drums. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The Merrie Monarch brought hula back.
img.title: KALAKAUA, MERRIE MONARCH

questions.question: Iolani Palace, completed in 1882 under Kalakaua, is famous in American history as:
questions.correctAnswer: The only royal palace on United States soil
distractors: The first skyscraper in the Pacific
questions.explanation: Iolani Palace housed the last monarchs; its modern features (electric light before the White House) symbolized the kingdom's ambition to stand among modern nations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: America's only royal palace.

questions.question: The constitution forced on Kalakaua in 1887 got the name 'Bayonet Constitution' because:
questions.correctAnswer: Armed militia backed the demand that he sign it or be deposed
distractors: It was written by army officers in a day
questions.explanation: In 1887 the Honolulu Rifles and a league of businessmen compelled Kalakaua to sign a constitution that weakened the king and shifted power to a cabinet answerable to the legislature.

questions.correctAnswer: Gave voting power to wealthy non-citizen residents while cutting many Native Hawaiian and all Asian voters out through income and property tests
distractors: Let women vote for the first time
questions.explanation: The 1887 constitution imposed property/income qualifications and a European-American oath, disenfranchising many Hawaiians and barring Asian residents entirely - power followed property.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1887: the vote followed property.

questions.question: The 1887 renewal of the Reciprocity Treaty gave the United States exclusive rights to use:
questions.correctAnswer: Pearl Harbor as a naval station
questions.explanation: The Pearl Harbor grant (1887) deepened US strategic interest in Hawaii - a fact annexationists used a decade later.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pearl Harbor enters the treaties: 1887.

questions.question: Liliuokalani became queen in 1891 after the death of her brother:
